claim.theorem: There is no finite simple bipartite graph G of minimum degree at least 3, with a bipartition class of size 19, that contains no simple cycle of length 4, 8, or 16.
claim.equivalent_part_size_form: Every finite simple bipartite graph of minimum degree at least 3 with no C4, C8, or C16 has both bipartition classes different from 19.
claim.direct_scope: The fixed side has 19 vertices; the opposite side is arbitrary. C4-freeness and minimum degree imply that it has at most C(19,2)/3 = 57 vertices, which is the exact finite encoding cap.

completeness_chain: Use the 19-vertex bipartition class as points and the neighborhoods of vertices in the other class as hyperedges.
Minimum degree makes every hyperedge have size at least 3 and every point have degree at least 3.
C4-freeness makes the hypergraph linear, so pair counting bounds the number of hyperedges by 57; unused prefix slots pad every instance to the fixed encoding.
The static quadrilateral clauses are equivalent to C8-freeness under the audited linear-incidence semantics.
Each learned clause forbids one exact simple alternating C16. Every stored block was independently decoded and checked.
The final CNF was reconstructed independently as the exact 381346-clause base followed by the exact 512 stored C16 blocks.

corollaries.standalone: Any bipartite Erdős-Gyárfás counterexample has neither bipartition class of size 19.
corollaries.combined_with_sigma_le_18_ladder: Together with the separately verified sigma <= 18 ladder, every bipartite Erdős-Gyárfás counterexample has at least 20 vertices in each class, hence at least 40 vertices in total.
